history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 519 (id ettumanoor-mahadeva-temple-kottayam). Ettumanoor Mahadeva Temple is a major Shiva shrine in Kottayam district, one of Kerala's principal Shiva temples alongside Vaikom and Kaduthuruthy (the three are traditionally visited on the same day). Present building with gopuram and fortifications was reconstructed in 717 ME (1542 AD). Famous for 16th-century Dravidian mural paintings, especially the Pradosha Nritham (Shiva's cosmic dance fresco); golden flagstaff topped with a Nandi bull; copper-plated roofs with 14 ornamental tops. Name origin traditions: Shiva appeared here in eight (ettu) forms (manam), or from 'manoor' (land of deer); deity Ettumanoorappan's name is traced to Kattampakk village. Legend: the asura Khara brought three lingas from Kailasa; installed by Parasurama. Believed Adi Shankaracharya composed the Soundarya Lahari while staying here. The Ezhara Ponnana - seven and a half gold elephant figures (nearly 13 kg), a Travancore king's donation - are displayed publicly only on the 8th and 10th days of the Arattu festival. One of the wealthiest Devaswoms in Kerala.

name: Ettumanoor Mahadeva Temple
town_description: Ettumanoor is a municipality in Kottayam district, about 12 km north of Kottayam city on the Kottayam-Vaikom-Ernakulam route. It is known chiefly for the Mahadeva temple, a major pilgrimage centre and home to celebrated 16th-century murals. The town sits in central Kerala's midland belt of paddy fields, coconut groves and rubber plantations, and serves as a stop on the Vaikom-Ettumanoor-Kaduthuruthy Shiva-temple circuit.
